summary: This week the team converged on a single execution chain: Safari login fix → rate-limit middleware refactor → CSV export v2. The Safari bug shipped Friday morning and customer reports stopped immediately. The rate-limit refactor is now the critical path because CSV export v2 cannot launch externally until the limiter survives instance restarts. CSV v2 design is final (tuple cursor + NDJSON + column selection); implementation lands behind a feature flag this week. Northwind ($200k ARR) is the headline customer waiting on CSV v2; expectations have been re-set from end-of-May to first half of June.
themes: Cross-browser auth hardening — Safari was a foreseeable miss; WebKit is now in CI.
Platform durability — middleware that doesn't survive instance restarts is the limiter on enterprise features.
CSV export v2 is enterprise-blocking — Northwind is gated, Beacon is gated.
Stale work needs to be closed, not nursed — PR #42 closed in favor of a fresh refactor.
Customer commitments are now sequenced honestly — Northwind moved from end-of-May to first half of June.

decisions.decision: Set Secure + SameSite=None on auth cookie and add WebKit to Playwright CI in the same PR (#188).
Sequence the work as: rate-limit refactor → CSV v2 external launch. CSV v2 implementation merges this week behind a feature flag in parallel.
CSV v2 cursor is a tuple of (created_at, id), not single-column created_at — single-column would skip rows on bursty timestamps.
Rate-limit refactor uses Redis-backed sliding window; token-bucket + Postgres advisory lock rejected as too novel for a one-week ship.
Close stale rate-limit PR #42 and start fresh — diff has rotted, tests aren't what we want.
Tell Northwind first half of June for CSV v2, not end of May. Honest sequencing given rate-limit risk.

blockers.blocker: Rate-limit middleware does not survive instance restart, blocking CSV v2 external launch and hitting limits during local CSV v2 testing.
Redis instance memory headroom at ~60%; new sliding-window keyspace may push it past the 75% comfort line — Lin to verify Friday.
Feb 2026 Safari postmortem action item 'add WebKit to Playwright CI' was deprioritized last quarter — direct cause of the May Safari outage.

open_questions: Should we collapse mail.acme-co.com and app.acme-co.com onto a single subdomain to eliminate cross-site cookie risk entirely? Deferred from the auth review — too much DNS surface to change mid-incident.
Do we need to bump the Redis instance size before launching the new sliding window? Lin to confirm by Friday.
Should we promise Beacon a Safari-fix retro-credit on their pilot? Not raised yet but probably the right move.
When do we make WebKit a required CI target (vs. nightly)? PR #188 adds it; we haven't decided whether it blocks merges yet.
